content.title: How to watch 2026 Oscars: Time, TV channel, free live stream
content.text: Updated: Mar. 15, 2026, 3:01 p.m.Published: Mar. 15, 2026, 3:00 p.m.FILE - Host Conan O'Brien speaks during the Oscars in Los Angeles on March 2, 2025.AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, FileIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Madison Kemeny | MKemeny@syracuse.comThe 98th Academy Awards (Oscars), hosted once again by Conan O’Brien, will air live from the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood on Sunday, March 15 on ABC.The awards show will be available to stream live on Fubo (5-day free trial), DIRECTV (5-day free trial) and more streaming services listed below.What time do the 2026 Oscars start?The 2026 Oscars air Sunday, March 15, at the new earlier start time of 7 p.m. ET. The official live red‑carpet show begins half an hour before the ceremony at 6:30 p.m. ET.What channel are the Oscars on?The 2026 Oscars will air live on ABC and stream live on Hulu.Where to watch the 2026 Oscars live and on demand for freeViewers without cable can watch the 2026 Oscars live and on demand for free by signing up for the trial offer from Fubo (free trial) or DIRECTV (free trial).Sling also carries ABC in select markets and offers a one-day pass for a one-time payment of $4.99. No commitment, no auto-renewal.The ceremony will also stream live on Hulu, which can be bundled with Disney+ for $4.99/month for the first three months for a limited time.Comparing streaming servicesFubo - Fubo offers one of the widest selections of channels among live TV streaming services. More than 220 channels, including all the sports and entertainment you love, plus sports add-ons for those niche networks you rely on. Plans start at $73.99/month, and it all starts with a free trial and up to $30 off the first month of service.FuboFree TrialStream the Oscars free for up to 5 days, and enjoy up to $30 off your first month.Free TrialDIRECTV - Watch live TV from major broadcast and popular cable networks. Enjoy local and national live sports, breaking news and must-see shows the moment they air. Included: unlimited cloud DVR storage space so you can record as many shows as you want and stream them from wherever you go. DTV starts as low as $19.99/month after a 5-day free trial when you shop their customizable genre packs.DIRECTV5-day free trialStream the Oscars free for 5 days, and enjoy up to $35 off your first month.Free TrialSling - One of the best deals in live TV streaming at just $45.99/month, offering customizable channel lineups for sports, news and entertainment. Now, Sling adds even more value with passes that let you stream live TV without a subscription: just $4.99 for a day, $9.99 for the weekend or $14.99 for a full week. These one-time payments are perfect if you just want to watch a single show, live game or special event. No commitment, no auto-renewal, just affordable access when you need it.Sling$60.99 $29.99Bundle Sling's Blue and Orange packages and get half off the first month of service.Claim OfferDisney+, Hulu Bundle - For a limited time, new and eligible returning subscribers can sign up for the Disney+ and Hulu bundle (With Ads) for just $4.99/month for the first three months, compared to the regular $12.99/month pricing. The promotion is live now and runs through March 24.Disney+, Hulu Bundle$12.99 $4.99Get Disney+, Hulu Bundle for the limited-time offer price of $4.99/month for 3 months.Claim OfferWith so many streaming platforms and shifting subscription prices, it’s always worth checking the latest free trials and promo deals to make sure you’re getting the best value when tuning in.‘The Real Housewives of Rhode Island’ premieres tonight: How to watch for freeNew evidence in John Wilkes Booth case to be revealed on ‘Expedition Files’ Season 4 tonightNew ‘Survivor 50′ Episode 6 airs tonight: Where to watch for free‘The Valley’ returns for Season 3 premiere tonight: How to watch for freeHow to secure Lily Allen presale tickets for fall tour dates before they sell outMadison Kemeny is a Commerce Reporter for syracuse.com | The Post-Standard, covering all things streaming and live entertainment.
